newsitem.title: USA: Clinton pokes fun at press corps, himself.
newsitem.headline: Clinton pokes fun at press corps, himself.

text.p: President Clinton gave journalists attending the annual White House Correspondents Dinner a brief jolt Saturday when he announced in his best deadpan manner that a balanced budget deal was imminent.
But before anyone abandoned their pricey dinner to run to the phones, the president delivered the punch line -- he thanked former Sen. Bob Dole for providing the $56 billion needed.

"Miraculously, the $56 billion gap that has separated Democrats and Republicans has been bridged and, ladies and gentlemen, we owe Sen. Dole a huge debt of gratitude," Clinton quipped. "The best part is we don't have to start paying it back until 2005."

Referring to reports of improper fund raising for his 1996 presidential campaign -- including the alleged use of private coffees for donors at the White House -- Clinton added, "You know, if I'd known Sen. Dole was that generous I'd have invited him over for coffee."

Former presidential candidate Dole recently gave his one-time rival, House Speaker Newt Gingrich, a $300,000 loan at 10 percent interest to pay a House ethics fine, with payments to begin in eight years.
Clinton poked fun at the White House press corps and their complaints about being notified late when he injured his knee in Florida last month.
"In the spirit of reinventing government ... starting tonight, we've decided to give you advance notice of impending mishaps," Clinton said, listing a few upcoming possible disasters.

The campaign finance controversy also provided fodder for the president. Halfway through his speech he had assistants wheel in a cart full of boxes, then chided the press for missing key stories contained in the thousands of documents recently released by his administration.
He read one memo in which former donors are offered an opportunity to meet Vice President Al Gore to discuss reinventing government, for a donation of $10,000.
"For $20,000, you don't have to go," he added with a sly smile, casting a glance at Gore.

Discussing his daughter, Chelsea, who will attend her first year of college next year, he said: "The bad news is our only child is going off to college; the good news is, it opens up another bedroom." Clinton has been criticised for allowing donors to stay overnight in the Lincoln Bedroom at the White House.

The annual dinner drew the usual crowds of politicians and Hollywood stars, including actor Alec Baldwin and his wife, actress Kim Basinger, as well as comedian Ellen Degeneres, who recently said publicly she was a lesbian.
